title: Common chunks and filtered approximation of Dwyer--Kan limit cones
statement:
Use combinatorial simplicial model categories and projective enriched diagram models of [lem-coef-simplicial-projective-model-calculus], and Dwyer--Kan homotopy limits and enriched localizations of [lem-coef-simplicial-localization-comparison-calculus]. Fix universes $\mathcal U\in\mathcal U'$; small in the following hypotheses means $\mathcal U$-small, and the full model category and the indexing collections of subcategories are allowed to fit in $\mathcal U'$. Let $\mathcal M$ be a combinatorial simplicial model category and $(I_a)_{a\in A}$ a small family of small cofibrant simplicial categories. A chunk $U\subseteq\mathcal M$ means a full simplicial subcategory with these closure properties, with choices functorial by enriched functors: every finite fan $X\to Y_i$ in $U$ has a factorization $X\to Z\to\prod_iY_i$ as a trivial cofibration followed by a fibration with $Z\in U$, and every finite cofan $Y_i\to X$ has a factorization $\coprod_iY_i\to Z\to X$ as a cofibration followed by a trivial fibration with $Z\in U$; empty families are included. For a small simplicial category $I$, $U^I$ denotes the full enriched subcategory of $\mathcal M^I$ of diagrams valued in $U$. An $I$-chunk means that $U$ is a chunk and $U^I$ is a chunk in the projective model structure.

Fix a small partially ordered set $K_0$. There is an infinite regular $\mathcal U$-small cardinal $\kappa$, which can be chosen depending only on $K_0$ and the Kan model on simplicial sets for the homotopy-limit clause below, with the following simultaneous approximation property. There is a $\mathcal U'$-small $\kappa$-filtered partially ordered collection of small full subcategories $U_\lambda\subseteq\mathcal M$, each a common $I_a$-chunk, whose union is $\mathcal M$. Here $\kappa$-filtered means that every subcollection of cardinality less than $\kappa$ has an upper bound. The collection can be required to be $\mu$-filtered for any prescribed infinite regular $\mathcal U$-small $\mu\geq\kappa$. For every $a$, full inclusions of subcategories induce a canonical Dwyer--Kan equivalence
$$\operatorname{colim}_\lambda\bigl(U_\lambda^{I_a}\cap(\mathcal M^{I_a})^f\bigr)[W_{\lambda,a}^{-1}]\longrightarrow(\mathcal M^{I_a})^f[W_a^{-1}],$$
where all the distinguished arrows are objectwise weak equivalences. The comparison is natural under enriched restriction between the $I_a$ and uses the actual restriction functors on fibrant diagrams.

Moreover the class of homotopy limit cones of shape $K_0^{\mathrm{op}}$ in $\mathrm{sCat}$ is stable under $\kappa$-filtered pointwise colimits: if $H_\lambda:K_0^{\mathrm{op}}\to\mathrm{sCat}$ and compatible cones $Z_\lambda\to H_\lambda$ are homotopy limit cones, then $\operatorname{colim}_\lambda Z_\lambda\to\operatorname{colim}_\lambda H_\lambda$ is a homotopy limit cone. The cardinal bound for this closure remains valid when the ambient universe is enlarged. Neither this assertion nor the approximation identifies simplicial categories with infinity categories.

source.place: Definition A.3.4.1 and Notation A.3.4.9 for the inline chunk and I-chunk definitions; Lemma A.3.4.15, printed pp.890-891, and the proof of Corollary A.3.6.18, printed p.905; accessible diagram factorizations from the proof of Proposition A.2.8.2. The localization comparison is the filtered-union step of that proof, using functorial enriched localization. Read online on 2026-10-17; archival copy WANTED. No Stacks tag states this enriched homotopy-theoretic result.

proof.text: Use the following finite-limit-sketch presentation of $\mathrm{sCat}$. Its sorts are the object set $O$ and, for every $n\geq0$, the set $A_n=\coprod_{x,y}C(x,y)_n$. The operations are source, target, faces, degeneracies, identities and composition on $A_n\times_OA_n$, with the category and simplicial identities. Thus the limit and filtered-colimit clause of [lem-coef-finite-limit-model-presentability] applies: limits and filtered colimits are formed on these sets. In particular, after representing two objects at a common stage, the mapping simplicial set between them in a filtered colimit is the filtered colimit of the eventual mapping simplicial sets. This last assertion follows by imposing the two endpoint equalities in each degree; equality in a filtered colimit is witnessed at a later stage by [lem-weil-pbc-filtered-colimit-sets-elementwise].

source.place: A.3.2, simplicial categories; elementary finite-limit-sketch and filtered-set calculation underlying the use of A.2.8.2 in A.3.6.18

proof.text: Consequently filtered pointwise colimits preserve Dwyer--Kan equivalences. Indeed, for objects represented in the source at a common stage, Step 1 identifies the map on mapping sets with a filtered colimit of weak homotopy equivalences, so [lem-coef-filtered-colimit-weak-equivalences] applies. Every target object is represented at a stage, where essential surjectivity supplies a source object and an isomorphism in the category of path components; its image is still an isomorphism in the colimit. Local weak equivalence and essential surjectivity are exactly the definition in [lem-coef-simplicial-localization-comparison-calculus]. This argument also allows transition functors that identify objects; it does not assume inclusions.

source.place: A.3.6.18 proof, filtered passage in Cat_S; elementary application of filtered invariance of simplicial-set weak equivalences

proof.text: Put $D=K_0^{\mathrm{op}}$. Apply [lem-coef-scat-diagram-factorization-uniform-bound] and factor each terminal arrow $H\to1$ as an injective trivial cofibration $H\to R_DH$ followed by an injective fibration. Thus $R_D$ is a functorial injective fibrant replacement. The constant terminal functor preserves filtered colimits because the index is nonempty and connected, so the asserted preservation for the middle-object functor makes $R_D$ preserve $\delta$-filtered colimits, with $\delta$ in the input universe uniformly in larger universes. Choose an infinite regular $\kappa\geq\delta$ with $|\operatorname{Mor}D|<\kappa$ using [lem-coef-small-family-regular-bound]. A $\kappa$-filtered index is also $\delta$-filtered. Both the bound and its preservation property depend only on $D$ and the fixed Kan-model/Bergner data, independently of $\mathcal M$ and $(I_a)$.

source.place: A.3.6.18 proof, first two cardinal-bound sentences; A.2.8.2 proof and A.1.2.5(2)

proof.text: For this $\kappa$, strict $D$-limits in $\mathrm{sCat}$ commute with pointwise $\kappa$-filtered colimits. On each sort of Step 1 an element of the limit is a compatible tuple, one element for each object of $D$. Represent these fewer than $\kappa$ elements at stages of the filtered diagram and choose a common receiving stage. For each arrow of $D$ the compatibility equality holds at a further stage by [lem-weil-pbc-filtered-colimit-sets-elementwise]; fewer than $\kappa$ arrows allow a common stage where they all hold. This proves surjectivity of the comparison. For injectivity do the same with the fewer than $\kappa$ coordinate equalities of two tuples. The resulting bijections commute with source, target and all operations, so are an isomorphism of simplicial categories by Step 1. For $D=\varnothing$ the tuple is empty and both sides are terminal: filtered index categories are nonempty and connected.

source.place: A.3.6.18 proof, fixed-shape filtered closure; elementary compatible-tuples calculation

proof.text:
Let $Z_t\to H_t$ be the compatible homotopy-limit cones in the statement. By [lem-coef-combinatorial-injective-diagram-model], their comparisons $c_t:Z_t\to\lim_D R_DH_t$ are Dwyer--Kan equivalences. They form a natural transformation because $R_D$ and its replacement map are functorial. Step 2 makes $\operatorname{colim}_t c_t$ a Dwyer--Kan equivalence. Steps 3--4 identify its target by canonical isomorphisms
$$\operatorname{colim}_t\lim_D R_DH_t\cong\lim_D\operatorname{colim}_tR_DH_t\cong\lim_D R_D(\operatorname{colim}_tH_t).$$
Compatibility of $\eta$ identifies the composite with the comparison of the colimit cone. The same injective-model criterion proves that cone homotopy limiting. This proves the entire fixed-shape clause, including the empty shape, with the uniform $\kappa$ of Step 3.

source.place: A.3.6.18 proof, fixed-shape homotopy-limit closure via the injective model of A.2.8.2

proof.text: For the chunk construction adjoin the one-object unit simplicial category to $(I_a)$ and index it by $*$. For every resulting $I_a$, [lem-coef-simplicial-projective-model-calculus] gives the combinatorial simplicial model category $\mathcal M^{I_a}$, with objectwise tensor, weak equivalences and fibrations. Choose its two enriched functorial factorizations by [lem-coef-enriched-functorial-factorizations]. The tensor hypothesis of that theorem holds: for any simplicial set $K$ and generating (trivial) cofibration $j$, $K\otimes j$ is a (trivial) cofibration, since all simplicial sets are cofibrant and the simplicial model axiom applies to $\varnothing\to K$. Fix these choices once for the whole categories, so restricting them to closed full subcategories will preserve inclusions. Let $F_a$ denote the middle object of the trivial-cofibration/fibration factorization and $G_a$ that of the cofibration/trivial-fibration factorization.

source.place: A.3.4.15 proof, first paragraph and the two enriched factorization functors; A.1.2.6

proof.text: Choose an infinite regular $\rho$ exceeding the cardinalities of the object sets of all the augmented $I_a$, by [lem-coef-small-family-regular-bound]. Given any small set $S$ of objects of $\mathcal M$, use [lem-weil-pbc-transfinite-recursion] to define increasing sets $S_\alpha$, $\alpha<\rho$: $S_0=S$, and at a nonzero limit take the union of earlier sets. At a successor retain $S_\alpha$ and add (i) every value of $F_a(u)$, where $u:f\to\prod_{i=1}^n g_i$ is a finite fan of diagrams valued in $S_\alpha$, and (ii) every value of $G_a(v)$, where $v:\coprod_{i=1}^n g_i\to f$ is a finite cofan of such diagrams. Include $n=0$ in both rules. Let $\mathrm{cl}(S)$ be the full simplicial subcategory on $\bigcup_{\alpha<\rho}S_\alpha$. These are exactly the successor operations in the construction of HTT A.3.4.15, now with globally fixed choices.

source.place: A.3.4.15 proof, transfinite construction (i)--(iii)(a)--(c), printed p.891

proof.text: Each $S_\alpha$ is small: a diagram on a small $I_a$ valued in a small full enriched subcategory is specified by small sets of choices of objects and maps between small mapping simplicial sets. The finite families and their enriched natural transformations therefore form a small set, and the successor rule adds only a small family of objects. Small unions at limits and at $\rho$ remain small. For a finite fan or cofan of diagrams valued in $\mathrm{cl}(S)$, its constituent values form a set of cardinality less than $\rho$. Regularity gives a single $\alpha<\rho$ containing all those values. Its chosen middle diagram has all values in $S_{\alpha+1}$ by construction. Fullness retains all maps between retained objects; the factorization maps to the ambient finite product or from the ambient finite coproduct are the ambient maps required by the chunk definition, and all enriched naturality maps are retained. Thus $\mathrm{cl}(S)^{I_a}$ is a chunk for every $a$. The added unit index gives the chunk condition on $\mathrm{cl}(S)$ itself. Empty fans and cofans give both replacements without requiring terminal or initial objects themselves to lie in the subcategory.

source.place: A.3.4.15 proof, verification of the transfinite construction; Definitions A.3.4.1 and A.3.4.9

proof.text: Let $P$ be the poset of all small full subcategories closed under the operations fixed in Step 6. It is a set in $\mathcal U'$: its object sets belong to the power set of the $\mathcal U'$-small object collection of $\mathcal M$. It is nonempty since it contains $\mathrm{cl}(\varnothing)$. For any $\mathcal U$-small subfamily of members of $P$, the union of their small object sets is small, and applying $\mathrm{cl}$ gives an upper bound in $P$. Hence $P$ is $\mu$-filtered for every prescribed infinite regular $\mathcal U$-small $\mu$, in particular for $\kappa$. Every object $X$ belongs to $\mathrm{cl}(\{X\})$, so its union is $\mathcal M$. Step 8 proves that every member is a common $I_a$-chunk. This proves the filtered-family clause rather than passing it to a new existence lemma.

source.place: A.3.6.18 proof, use of A.3.4.15 to form a filtered union; explicit poset and upper bounds

proof.text: For each $a$ put $C_{\lambda,a}=U_\lambda^{I_a}\cap(\mathcal M^{I_a})^f$ and $C_a=(\mathcal M^{I_a})^f$, with their actual enriched mapping sets. Every object of $C_a$ has a small set of values, so those values belong to a single member of $P$ by Step 9. Each $C_{\lambda,a}$ is full in $C_a$, whence their enriched union is exactly $C_a$. Between objects present at a stage the full mapping simplicial set is already present, so the same holds for its weak-equivalence vertices: $W_a$ is the union of $W_{\lambda,a}$. Objectwise fibrancy and weak equivalence are exactly the projective classes supplied by [lem-coef-simplicial-projective-model-calculus].

source.place: A.3.6.18 proof, passage from small common chunks to the full diagram categories

proof.text: To compute the enriched localization functorially, use its homotopy-pushout definition in [lem-coef-simplicial-localization-comparison-calculus]. For a pair $(C,W)$ write its span as $B\leftarrow A\to E$, where $B=C$, $A=\coprod_W[1]$ and $E=\coprod_W J$. Apply [lem-coef-scat-diagram-factorization-uniform-bound] with the terminal index category to choose ordinary functorial cofibration/trivial-fibration factorizations in $\mathrm{sCat}$ whose middle-object functor preserves $\epsilon$-filtered colimits for some regular $\epsilon\in\mathcal U$, even in the enlarged ambient universe. First factor $\varnothing\to A$ to obtain $QA\xrightarrow{\sim}A$. Factor each composite $QA\to B$ and $QA\to E$ to obtain cofibrations $QA\to QB,QE$ and trivial fibrations $QB\to B$, $QE\to E$. The resulting span $QB\leftarrow QA\to QE$ is Reedy cofibrant and is objectwise weakly equivalent to the original span by [lem-coef-reedy-model-structure].

source.place: A.3.5.1 localization, interpreted as a derived pushout; A.1.2.5 and the direct Reedy model of A.2.9

proof.text: The pushout $L(C,W)=QB\amalg_{QA}QE$ computes that homotopy pushout. Indeed the span category is direct Reedy, so its fibrations are objectwise; the constant diagram functor therefore preserves fibrations and trivial fibrations. Its left adjoint, pushout, is left Quillen, and its value on the Reedy cofibrant replacement of Step 11 is the derived pushout. This is the localization model we use for every pair, with all transition functors induced by the same construction. It avoids choosing unrelated representatives of homotopy pushouts.

source.place: A.3.5.1; A.2.9, direct Reedy calculation of a derived pushout

proof.text:
Choose a regular $\mu\geq\kappa,\epsilon$ in $\mathcal U$ (and at least any prescribed regular lower bound), using [lem-coef-small-family-regular-bound]. Step 9 makes $P$ $\mu$-filtered. Every operation forming the replacement span in Step 11 preserves these colimits: the middle-object functor does so, and the constant initial object does because the index is filtered. Also $W\mapsto\coprod_W[1]$ and $W\mapsto\coprod_WJ$ preserve colimits of sets, by the universal property of coproducts. Colimits commute with pushouts, since maps from either iterated colimit to a test object are exactly the same compatible cocones. With the union identities of Step 10 this gives a canonical isomorphism
$$\operatorname{colim}_\lambda L(C_{\lambda,a},W_{\lambda,a})\cong L(C_a,W_a).$$
In particular the displayed comparison of localizations in the statement is a Dwyer--Kan equivalence. A functorial weakly equivalent localization model gives the same conclusion, because Step 2 preserves its stagewise comparisons.

source.place: A.3.6.18 proof, filtered localization passage; A.1.2.5(2) and the localization span of A.3.5.1

proof.text: Finally let $v:I_a\to I_b$ be any enriched restriction map. Precomposition sends a diagram valued in $U_\lambda$ to one valued in the same $U_\lambda$ and preserves objectwise fibrancy and weak equivalences. It therefore gives actual functors of the pairs $(C_{\lambda,b},W_{\lambda,b})\to(C_{\lambda,a},W_{\lambda,a})$ and of the full pairs. Functoriality of Step 11 makes their localization squares commute, and the colimit comparison in Step 13 is induced by these commuting squares. This proves the asserted restriction naturality, even when restriction fails to preserve projective cofibrancy. The only bound used in Steps 3--5 is the uniform replacement bound for $D$ and the cardinality of its arrows, so it remains valid in larger universes. The family construction and the possible larger $\mu$ impose no dependence on $\mathcal M$ on that homotopy-limit bound. No passage to a coherent nerve has occurred.

source.place: A.3.6.18 proof, actual restrictions on fibrant diagrams and the universe-invariance sentence
